male.name: The Chikkodi cane cutter
male.tagline: A landless cane cutter who migrates each October with his wife, on a mukadam's advance.

dayInLife.text: Takes a cash advance from the mukadam and heads to the sugar factories with his wife.
The couple cuts cane with the koyta blade to avoid the worst heat.
They load bullock carts or tractors bound for the factory weighbridge.
The family lives in a makeshift tarpaulin shelter near the field or factory.
Back home for daily-wage farm work and a small leased plot of jowar or cotton.

topics.label: Daily Life & Work
topics.headline: Paired cane-cutting for six months, then daily-wage work at home
points: Each October a mukadam advances cash and recruits koyta pairs for factories in Belagavi, Kolhapur and Sangli.
Wages are calculated by tonnage cut, with no written contract, fixed hours or formal safety net.
May to September means daily-wage farm work and a small leased plot of jowar or cotton.

stat.label: cane-cutting season each year, October to April

topics.label: Family & Household
topics.headline: A joint family split by migration
points: He, his wife, two children and elderly parents share one home in the native village.
While the couple migrates, his parents stay behind to manage the children and the small plot.
His priority for now is to delay both children's marriages until they finish school.

stat.label: child-marriage cases in Belagavi in 2024-25, second-highest in Karnataka

topics.label: Education & Schooling
topics.headline: Keeping both children in school past Class 8 is the goal
points: His own schooling ended after Class 7, as is common in cane-cutting families.
His son, nearing Class 9, has missed stretches of school when he could not stay with his grandmother.
His daughter attends the local Kannada-medium government school and stays with her grandmother during migration months.

topics.label: Health & Wellbeing
topics.headline: Injury is the constant risk, with no safety net
points: Cutting cane with the koyta blade causes frequent hand and leg cuts and chronic back and joint pain.
In season the family lives in a tarpaulin lean-to without reliable clean water, toilets or a nearby clinic.
He rarely has the documents or time to enrol in Arogya Karnataka; there is no paid leave or insurance.

topics.label: Community & Belief
topics.headline: A Kuruba family, held together by a migrant labour network
points: Kurubas are an Other Backward Classes group, counted at roughly 7.5% of Karnataka in the 2015 survey.
Families from neighbouring villages migrate under one mukadam, pooling money for emergencies and informal childcare.
They occasionally visit the Saundatti Yellamma fair and mark Kittur Utsav each October, recalling Rani Chennamma's 1824 revolt.

stat.label: Kuruba share of Karnataka's population, 2015 survey placed before cabinet April 2025

topics.label: Civic Life & Government
topics.headline: Mostly dealing with the mukadam, not the state
points: He holds a ration card and an MGNREGA job card, used for off-season village wage work.
His wife and daughter ride free on state buses under Shakti; his son expects the new student bus pass.
Contact with panchayats is limited; the cane season often keeps him away from election campaigns and polling day.

stat.label: a tonne announced after the November 2025 strike (farmers sought Rs 3,500)

topics.label: Worldview & Concerns
topics.headline: Debt is the deepest worry, then schooling and cane prices
points: The mukadam's advance binds the family to one contractor and can take years to repay.
He takes pride in the work's toughness, in providing for his family, and in Kitturu Karnataka's identity.
He would want hostel seats for migrant children, a cane price fixed early, and health camps at labour camps.

schoolPressures.label: Cane migration
schoolPressures.detail: Six months away takes parents, and sometimes older children, from home across two school terms.

schoolPressures.label: Cane-cutting work
schoolPressures.detail: He fears his son, old enough to be a second hand in a koyta pair, will leave before Class 10.

schoolPressures.label: No camp schools
schoolPressures.detail: The High Court ordered tent schools and seasonal hostels near labour camps, but implementation is patchy.

schoolPressures.label: Debt and costs
schoolPressures.detail: The mukadam's advance and the cane price decide whether school fees and uniforms can be met.

female.name: The Lambani tanda labourer
female.tagline: A Lambani mother holding the household together while her husband works in Goa or Pune.

dayInLife.text: She rises to fetch water and prepare the household's morning meal.
She walks or cycles to whichever grape, pomegranate or cotton field is hiring that week.
Without field work she does MGNREGA earthwork at whichever site the gram panchayat opens.
Cooking, water collection and care of her two children fall almost entirely on her.
Her husband's remittances from Goa or Pune arrive irregularly, so she cannot budget around them.

topics.label: Daily Life & Work
topics.headline: Day-wage fieldwork, MGNREGA earthwork and a double burden
points: She works wherever grape, pomegranate or cotton fields are hiring, paid by the day, following the vineyard calendar.
When farm work is scarce she takes MGNREGA earthwork at whichever site the gram panchayat opens.
Her husband's irregular remittances are the main cushion, alongside a monthly state cash transfer.

stat.label: of Karnataka's annual MGNREGA person-days used within six months, 2023 drought

topics.label: Family & Household
topics.headline: Women run the household while men migrate
points: She lives with her two children and her husband's parents in a one- or two-room kutcha house in the tanda.
She and her mother-in-law decide daily food, schooling and healthcare; big decisions wait for her husband's visits.
Her teenage daughter already helps with cooking, fetching water and minding her younger brother.

stat.label: tandas (Lambani hamlets) in Karnataka, typically set apart from the main village

topics.label: Education & Schooling
topics.headline: Getting her daughter to Class 9 and beyond
points: Her own schooling stopped around Class 5, common among women of her generation in Lambani tandas.
Tandas typically have only a primary school nearby; high school means travelling several kilometres to a town like Indi.
Vijayapura's Class 10 pass rate was 94.16% in 2026; her worry is her daughter reaching the exam at all.

stat.label: female literacy in Vijayapura district versus 77.2% for men, 2011 Census

topics.label: Health & Wellbeing
topics.headline: Fluoride in the water and no cushion for emergencies
points: A study of Indi taluk borewells found just over half exceeding the safe fluoride limit, rising over time.
Her tanda drinks borewell water; neither she nor her children have a formal fluorosis diagnosis.
A trip to the taluk hospital costs a full day's wages; she has had no recent health check-up.

stat.label: mean fluoride in borewells across 22 Indi taluk villages

topics.label: Community & Belief
topics.headline: Lambani identity in a tanda that largely looks after itself
points: The Lambani (Banjara) community, of nomadic origin, is grouped within Scheduled Castes in Karnataka, a classification its leaders contest.
Elders and a community head settle disputes and organise weddings; the tanda shares childcare while men migrate.
Women in her tanda practise Lambani embroidery, mostly for household and ceremonial use rather than cash income.

topics.label: Civic Life & Government
topics.headline: Gruha Lakshmi, MGNREGA and free buses are her contact with the state
points: Gruha Lakshmi pays Rs 2,000 a month to women heads of low-income households, though payments run late.
She holds an MGNREGA job card, used when field labour is unavailable, especially in drought periods.
Shakti free bus travel eases her trips; she expects her daughter to use the new student bus pass from 2026-27.

stat.label: allocated to Gruha Lakshmi in the 2026-27 state budget

topics.label: Worldview & Concerns
topics.headline: Water, her daughter's schooling and unreliable support
points: Her biggest daily worry is reliable, safe drinking water from borewells in a fluoride-affected belt.
She would want a school or hostel seat nearer the tanda, safe transport and reliable student-pass delivery.
She takes pride in embroidery and in running the household alone for months, but calls it necessity, not preference.

schoolPressures.label: Distance to school
schoolPressures.detail: Only primary schools are nearby; Class 9 means daily travel to a town high school.

schoolPressures.label: Care work
schoolPressures.detail: With her mother in the fields and father away, her daughter is relied on for cooking and sibling care.

schoolPressures.label: Fluoride in water
schoolPressures.detail: Elevated fluoride in Indi taluk borewells is linked to joint pain and deformities that can reduce school attendance.

schoolPressures.label: Early marriage
schoolPressures.detail: Early marriage is a live risk at the Class 8-10 age, especially if the household hits a financial crisis.
